editorial_reason: ProofWiki defines a graph intuitively through vertices and edges, then distinguishes directed, multigraph and loop conventions. This source is not itself a sufficiently specific standalone formal graph type to justify equivalence with every graph convention.

contextual_variant_leads: finite simple graph adds finite V
nonempty simple graph adds V not empty
simple graph including possible empty V
editorial_reason: ProofWiki formal simple-graph definition specifies antireflexive symmetric adjacency and equivalent unordered doubleton edges. The same page notes that some authors require V to be finite or nonempty, but these restrictions are not imposed in the general version.

contextual_variant_leads: pseudograph or loop-multigraph requires explicit loop conventions
editorial_reason: ProofWiki's multigraph definition explicitly allows multiple copies of an unordered pair of vertices and represents E as a multiset of doubletons. This convention has no loops. Different sources allow loops and use edge identities plus incidence maps; those must be separate variants.
